summary: An [ICT sector strategic plan](2025-01-01-minict-rwanda-ict-sector-strategic-plan-2024-2029) covering 2024/25 to 2028/29 replaced the 2018 to 2024 plan, and only a front-matter extract is held.
developments:
The plan is the standing sector instrument and the base holds a front-matter extract rather than the body, so the artefact is the record and its targets cannot be quoted against outturn ([plan](2025-01-01-minict-rwanda-ict-sector-strategic-plan-2024-2029)).

It is also what dates the data centre and cloud directives, which carry no date of their own. A strategy whose text the base cannot read is a limit on every judgement in this report about whether delivery is on plan.

summary: The [national broadband policy](2025-10-22-digital-penetration-masterclass-telecomreview) was revised in 2022, abandoning the single-wholesale-network model, and a [phased legacy-network retirement plan](2026-07-30-rwanda-3g-sunset-2027) now dates the third-generation sunset to June 2027.
developments:
The revision abandoned the single-wholesale-network model the country had been known for ([policy](2025-10-22-digital-penetration-masterclass-telecomreview)).

Government approved a phased retirement plan for the older networks; in March 2026 the ministry had opened talks with device importers with no firm timeline, and the plan is what replaced that ([plan](2026-07-30-rwanda-3g-sunset-2027), [sunset](2026-07-28-rwanda-minict-3g-2g-network-sunset)).

The third-generation switch-off is dated 30 June 2027 by the ministry, and the stated rationale is operator cost and spectrum rather than consumer benefit ([third generation](2026-07-29-rwanda-june-2027-deadline-retire-3g), [phase-out](2026-03-30 Rwanda Moves to Phase Out 2G and 3G Devices in Digital Transition Push)). December 2028 is a working target for the second-generation switch-off, and a commissioned study puts more than two million people still on the older network in 2030 absent a planned transition ([second generation](2026-07-30-rwanda-3g-sunset-2027)).

summary: A [national artificial-intelligence policy](2026-07-30-cipit-east-african-ai-policy-outlook-report) was approved by cabinet in April 2023, and a [national agency](2026-06-08-ai-agency-cabinet-approves-ktpress) was approved in June 2026 with no establishing instrument published.
developments:
The policy has been in force since April 2023 and is the instrument every later commitment is read against ([policy](2026-07-30-cipit-east-african-ai-policy-outlook-report), [outlook](2026-06-08-ai-agency-cabinet-approves-ktpress)).

Cabinet approved a dedicated agency in June 2026 and a coordinating mandate for shared compute was stated in August; software developers and early-stage startups welcomed it in the national press and set out what they want from it, compute and infrastructure improvements and expanded room for commercialisation. That is a statement of the gaps the sector reports rather than of the agency's remit: no establishing instrument, budget, staffing or timetable is held, so the base cannot say whether any of it falls to the agency at all ([agency](2026-06-08-ai-agency-cabinet-approves-ktpress), [startups](2026-08-17-newtimes-ai-agency-startups), [gaps](2026-08-17-rwanda-startups-national-ai-agency-infrastructure-gaps)).

summary: A [national data-sharing policy](2025-10-27 Introduction to the Rwanda National Data Sharing Policy) approved in 2025 runs open by default with a safe-access framework, and [implementation](2026-05-07 What will determine the success of Rwanda’s data governance push) began after cabinet approval in May 2025.
developments:
The policy is open by default with a safe-access framework, governance sitting with the statistics office and the platform with the information society authority ([policy](2025-10-27 Introduction to the Rwanda National Data Sharing Policy), [course](2025-06-09 Rwanda charts a new course for government data sharing)).

Implementation is under way and the policy text and its seven annexes are not held, so what the safe-access framework actually requires of a controller cannot be stated here ([implementation](2026-05-07 What will determine the success of Rwanda’s data governance push), [governance](2025-10-27 Introduction to the Rwanda National Data Sharing Policy)).

It is the clearest instance in this unit of a pattern that recurs: the instrument is announced and summarised, and the text that would let anyone check the summary is not published.

summary: A [national digital public infrastructure strategy](2026-03-11-dpi-strategy-launch-newtimes) was launched at a first national infrastructure day in March 2026, and the strategy document itself is not held.
developments:
The launch was at the country's first national digital public infrastructure day in March 2026, framed as laying groundwork for artificial intelligence and inclusive growth ([strategy](2026-03-11-dpi-strategy-launch-newtimes), [launch](2026-03-20 Rwanda Launches Digital Public Infrastructure Strategy to Lay Groundwork for AI and Inclusive Growth)).

The document is not held, so its sequencing, targets and financing cannot be checked against the identity, payments and data-sharing components that are separately recorded here.

summary: The [data protection and privacy law](2026-01-26-year-of-accountability-data-controllers-newtimes) has been fully in force since a two-year grace period ended in October 2023, and the Act's own text and law number are not held.
developments:
The grace period ended on 15 October 2023, and the authority's framing of the period since is a year of accountability for controllers ([law](2026-01-26-year-of-accountability-data-controllers-newtimes), [expansion](2026-05-18 Africa’s Digital Economy Is Expanding Faster than Its Privacy Protections)).

Neither the Act's text nor its law number is held. What the base can say about the regime is therefore drawn from secondary accounts of it and from the appropriation lines that fund the supervisory authority.

summary: A [single digital identification law](2026-03-26-govt-sets-2027-deadline-digital-id-newtimes) writes a June 2027 sunset of all legacy documents into statute, and the law's number and enactment date are not held.
developments:
The sunset is written into the law rather than set by administrative decision, which is what makes the enrolment count a legal deadline rather than a target ([deadline](2026-03-26-govt-sets-2027-deadline-digital-id-newtimes), [enrolment](2025-08-08 Rwanda National Identification Agency begins digital ID enrollment)).

The law's number and enactment date are not held, so the base cannot say what it provides on correction, appeal or exclusion for anyone unenrolled when legacy documents cease to be valid.

summary: The lower house approved the rationale for a [draft law on virtual assets](2026-04-01-virtual-assets-draft-law-techafricanews) in April 2026 with nothing reported since, above a [central bank regulatory sandbox](2026-06-19 Strategy Ahead of Infrastructure, Part II The Opportunity and the Case for Sequencing) established in 2022.
developments:
The chamber approved the rationale in April 2026 and nothing has been reported on the draft since ([draft](2026-04-01-virtual-assets-draft-law-techafricanews)).

The sandbox has run since 2022 on an analyst's account; its own regulation is not held, so its admission criteria, cohort and exit route are unstated ([sandbox](2026-06-19 Strategy Ahead of Infrastructure, Part II The Opportunity and the Case for Sequencing)).

summary: No [review framework for commercial artificial-intelligence partnerships](2026-03-17 Anthropic is Becoming the Backbone of Rwanda's Government. But Who is Accountable) is held, and a three-year vendor memorandum was signed in February 2026 without one.
developments:
External commentary asks who is accountable when a frontier vendor becomes infrastructure for government health and education work, and records that the memorandum was signed with no review framework in place; the criticism is attributed, not adopted ([commentary](2026-03-17 Anthropic is Becoming the Backbone of Rwanda's Government. But Who is Accountable), [memorandum](2026-02-17-anthropic-rwanda-mou-ai-health-education)).

The country holds an artificial-intelligence policy and is standing up an agency, so the gap is specifically in the instrument that would govern a commercial partnership rather than in artificial-intelligence policy generally.

summary: A [supervisory authority](2026-01-26-year-of-accountability-data-controllers-newtimes) is named under the 2021 law, and its [appropriation held flat](2026-06-30-rwa-2026-01-fr) in 2026/27 at about US$114,000 on the 2024/25 rate.
developments:
The authority is the named supervisor under the law ([authority](2026-01-26-year-of-accountability-data-controllers-newtimes), [finance law](2026-06-30-rwa-2026-01-fr)).

Its appropriation was held flat in the 2026/27 finance law, at about US$114,000 on the 2024/25 exchange rate — a supervisory function for the whole economy funded at roughly the cost of a small office ([appropriation](2026-06-30-rwa-2026-01-fr), [prior year](2025-06-30-rwa-2025-01-fr), [baseline](2024-06-26-rwa-2024-01-fr)).

Nothing on file records an enforcement action, penalty or audit by it at any date.

summary: A [registration regime for controllers and processors](2026-01-26-year-of-accountability-data-controllers-newtimes) has run since the 2021 law, and the authority's own framing is that registration is the beginning rather than the end.
developments:
The regime has been live since the law and the authority itself says registration is where compliance starts ([regime](2026-01-26-year-of-accountability-data-controllers-newtimes)).

A civil-society privacy scorecard, in its fifth edition, is the other measure the base holds, and it carries no country-specific figure for 2024 ([scorecard](2026-05-18 Africa’s Digital Economy Is Expanding Faster than Its Privacy Protections)). Between a registration count that measures enrolment rather than practice and a scorecard with no figure for this country, readiness here is asserted more than it is measured.

progress: Mixed, a bilateral health agreement signed while the data-sharing arrangement under it is unpublished
summary: A [United States bilateral health agreement](2025-12-05-afghs-mou-rwanda) was signed in Washington in December 2025, and the [data-sharing arrangement under it](2026-06-08-hrw-human-rights-assessment-afghs-bilateral-health-agreements) is not published.
developments:
The agreement was signed by the foreign minister and its text republished by a public-interest organisation; it states itself to be non-binding ([agreement](2025-12-05-afghs-mou-rwanda)).

The arrangement governing data under it is not published. What the base holds is a rights organisation's reading of the signed memorandum text, so the terms on which health and specimen data would move are known only through one organisation's account of a document the parties have not released ([reading](2026-06-08-hrw-human-rights-assessment-afghs-bilateral-health-agreements)).

That is the whole of the record: a signed instrument whose operative annexe nobody outside the parties has seen.

summary: The capital hosted [country consultations for a regional artificial-intelligence framework](2026-08-04-rwanda-highlights-ai-policy-progress-as-comesa-seeks-regional-framework) in August 2026, and it adopted a [continental declaration](2025-04-04 Africa Declaration on Artificial Intelligence) in April 2025 whose signatory count is disputed.
developments:
The consultations ran under a regional body's programme in August 2026 ([consultations](2026-08-04-rwanda-highlights-ai-policy-progress-as-comesa-seeks-regional-framework)), and a separate regional policy roadmap was explored at a science conference in March 2026 with no text, timetable or secretariat named ([roadmap](2026-03-31 EAC moves to create unified AI Sovereignty bloc)).

The continental declaration was adopted in the capital in April 2025, is non-binding, and its signatory count is disputed across three sources ([declaration](2025-04-04 Africa Declaration on Artificial Intelligence), [uncertainty](2025-05-13 Optimism but uncertainty over Africa's AI Declaration)).

One edition of the global summit that produced it has been held ([summit](2025-04-04 Africa Declaration on Artificial Intelligence)). The country's convening record is strong and none of the four instruments has a published output.

summary: A [bilateral licence passporting memorandum](2025-02-26-bank-of-ghana-press-release-ghana-rwanda-mou-licence-passporting) was signed in February 2025 and its text is unpublished, and a [second passporting framework](2026-03-12-kenya-rwanda-fintech-licence-passporting-techcabal) was agreed with another neighbour in March 2026.
developments:
The first memorandum was signed between the two central banks in February 2025 and its text has not been published ([memorandum](2025-02-26-bank-of-ghana-press-release-ghana-rwanda-mou-licence-passporting), [compliance cost](2026-07-30-the-compliance-cost-can-africa-build-a-regulatory-home-for-its-fintechs)).

The second was signed in March 2026; the earlier bilateral memorandum predates it and its text is still unpublished, so a firm cannot read either instrument to find out what passporting actually confers ([framework](2026-03-12-kenya-rwanda-fintech-licence-passporting-techcabal)).

Two unpublished memoranda are the whole of the regional licensing record, and no firm is reported as having used either.

summary: A [cross-border digital identity pilot](2026-08-11-giz-smart-africa-digital-sovereignty-interview) runs with two other states, a [terrestrial fibre route](2026-02-09-paratus-goma-mombasa-fibre-highway-itweb) was switched on in February 2026, and a [regional satellite study](2026-08-24-chimpreports-ncip-partner-state-communications-satellite-study) opened a joint funding account.
developments:
The identity pilot runs through a continental alliance with German development cooperation, and no scale, service, date or governing instrument is stated ([pilot](2026-08-11-giz-smart-africa-digital-sovereignty-interview)).

The fibre route was reported switched on in February 2026; the account is a vendor press release republished verbatim with no independent confirmation the route is live, and the corridor length and network footprint are the operator's own ([route](2026-02-09-paratus-goma-mombasa-fibre-highway-itweb), [forum](2026-08-18-paratus-rwanda-afpif-2026)).

Partner states opened a joint funding account for a communications satellite feasibility study with deposits due 30 September 2026, and neither the study's cost nor each state's share was disclosed ([study](2026-08-24-chimpreports-ncip-partner-state-communications-satellite-study)).

summary: A [government-wide enterprise architecture framework](2026-08-06-risa-government-of-rwanda-enterprise-architecture-framework-v2-1) stands as the functional equivalent of an interoperability framework, and only an excerpt of version 2.1 is held.
developments:
The framework document was acquired as an excerpt in August 2026, so it is present in the base as an artefact rather than as a readable standard ([framework](2026-08-06-risa-government-of-rwanda-enterprise-architecture-framework-v2-1)).

A reference study of interoperability challenges in the public sector is cited rather than absorbed ([study](2019-10-01 E-Government Systems Interoperability Challenges - Public Sector in Rwanda (Mugumya, MSc thesis))). The gap the country's own analysts name most often is the data-sharing platform rather than the standard, which is recorded separately.

summary: The capital hosted a [technical assessment mission for cross-border data-exchange conformance](2026-04-27 Smart Africa drives cross-border data interoperability through SADX Technical Mission) in April 2026, as host and participant rather than as owner of the framework.
developments:
The mission drove cross-border data interoperability under a continental alliance's exchange framework ([mission](2026-04-27 Smart Africa drives cross-border data interoperability through SADX Technical Mission)).

The framework itself belongs on the region's ledger rather than this one, so what the country has here is participation and a conformance assessment, not an adopted national standard. No conformance result is published.

summary: An [internet governance forum](2026-07-30-digital-trust-ai-oversight-rwanda-internet-governance-forum) convened its 2026 edition in July on digital trust and artificial-intelligence oversight, with no outcome document held.
developments:
The edition convened on 30 July 2026 around digital trust and oversight of artificial intelligence ([forum](2026-07-30-digital-trust-ai-oversight-rwanda-internet-governance-forum)), with a parallel strand on young people shaping the country's digital future ([young voices](2026-07-27-young-voices-shaping-rwandas-digital-future)).

No outcome document, government commitment or first-edition date is held, so the forum registers here as a convening rather than as an input the base can trace into an instrument.

summary: The [information and communications for development appropriation](2026-06-30-rwa-2026-28-98) fell for a third year running and the programme is now 93 per cent externally financed, while the [science and innovation appropriation](2026-06-30-rwa-2026-01-19) also fell.
developments:
Domestic appropriation for the development programme fell a third year running and external financing now carries 93 per cent of it and rising ([appropriation](2026-06-30-rwa-2026-28-98), [prior](2025-06-30-rwa-2025-28-98), [baseline](2024-06-26-rwa-2024-28-98)).

The science, technology and innovation appropriation also fell in the 2026/27 finance law; the programme is broader than digital and the digital share is not separable ([science](2026-06-30-rwa-2026-01-19), [year before](2025-06-30-rwa-2025-01-19)).

The direction is consistent across the digital lines the finance law carries: the delivery record in this unit rests on external money, and the domestic share is shrinking as it does.

summary: The [digital acceleration project](2025-07-09-rdap-fast-track-2026-newtimes) stood at 55 per cent complete in July 2025, and [two financing agreements](2026-08-21-newtimes-rwanda-rwf279bn-financing-jobs-broadband) for broadband and labour-market systems were approved unanimously in August 2026.
developments:
The acceleration project is the largest connectivity instrument in the base and the one with the stalest reporting, last recorded at 55 per cent complete in July 2025 ([project](2025-07-09-rdap-fast-track-2026-newtimes), [appraisal](2021-11-30-wb-rwa-001-digital-acceleration-project)).

The chamber approved two financing agreements for broadband and labour-market systems in August 2026; the digital share of the combined total is not itemised and no disbursement or procurement is on record ([agreements](2026-08-21-newtimes-rwanda-rwf279bn-financing-jobs-broadband), [approval](2026-08-21-radiotv10-rwanda-two-loans-rwf279-billion)).

A regional bank's digital acceleration operation, its first digital investment in the sub-region, runs 2022 to 2026 ([operation](2021-01-01-aiib-rwa-digital-acceleration-2021-rwanda-digital-acceleration-project-digital-investment)), and a nine-year country partnership framework is prepared but not formally launched ([framework](2026-07-30-world-bank-nine-year-rwanda-financing-framework)).

summary: A development institution committed [US$44.4m to shared tower investment](2025-01-01-bii-rwa-001-paradigm-tower-ventures-investment-shared-telecom), a [venture debt fund](2026-08-03-rwanda-development-bank-venture-debt-fund) is in development and not closed, and a [digital investment roadmap](2025-10-30-digital-fdi-report-techafricanews) has produced no enacted reform.
developments:
The tower commitment was made in September 2025 into a multi-market vehicle, with no country-specific tower count held ([towers](2025-01-01-bii-rwa-001-paradigm-tower-ventures-investment-shared-telecom)).

The venture debt fund is not closed and the account is the fund manager's own, with the event date unestablished ([fund](2026-08-03-rwanda-development-bank-venture-debt-fund)).

The investment roadmap was launched at an investment conference in October 2025 and no reform has been reported as enacted since ([roadmap](2025-10-30-digital-fdi-report-techafricanews)). Startup funding for 2025 is recorded by a tracker report that gives no prior-year comparator for this country ([funding](2026-02-03-disrupt-africa-african-tech-startups-funding-report-2025)), so the direction of private capital here is not measurable from what the base holds.

summary: A [capital-markets registrar-services memorandum](2026-08-07-rwanda-cma-africa-prudential-capital-markets-mou) was signed in August 2026 with no term or value published, and the head of state [co-chairs a global artificial-intelligence commission](2026-07-03 Kagame co-chairs global AI commission).
developments:
The registrar-services memorandum was signed in August 2026; no term, value or workplan is published and no investor-data protection provision is reported ([memorandum](2026-08-07-rwanda-cma-africa-prudential-capital-markets-mou)).

The head of state was confirmed as co-chair of a global commission in July 2026, and no national work programme or output is attached to the seat ([commission](2026-07-03 Kagame co-chairs global AI commission)).

A bilateral artificial-intelligence memorandum with a North African state was signed at a United Nations summit in July 2026 and its text is not held ([bilateral](2026-07-10-rwanda-egypt-ai-mou-techafricanews)). The pattern across all three is a signature the base can date and an instrument it cannot read.

summary: [Regulator quarterly statistics](2026-06-29-rura-ict-sector-statistics-report-q1-2026) carry mobile and internet subscriptions to the first quarter of 2026, and [voice over fourth-generation networks](2026-08-03-mtn-rwanda-volte-rollout) launched in August 2026.
developments:
The regulator's quarterly report is the subscription series, and it carries no printed publication date ([statistics](2026-06-29-rura-ict-sector-statistics-report-q1-2026)).

Voice over fourth-generation networks launched in August 2026. It is the technical precondition for retiring circuit-switched voice, though the source makes no reference to the sunset ([voice](2026-08-03-mtn-rwanda-volte-rollout)).

The fifth-generation network launched in June 2025 and nothing on the build has entered the base in the fourteen months since ([fifth generation](2025-06-12 Rwanda hits 38% internet penetration, but cost still keeps millions offline)).

summary: An international body put [mid-2025 internet penetration at 38 per cent](2025-06-12 Rwanda hits 38% internet penetration, but cost still keeps millions offline) with end-2025 projected at 42.6, and the most recent figure the base holds is a projection rather than a measurement.
developments:
Penetration was measured at 38 per cent in mid-2025 and 42.6 per cent for end-2025 is a projection ([penetration](2025-06-12 Rwanda hits 38% internet penetration, but cost still keeps millions offline), [masterclass](2025-10-22-digital-penetration-masterclass-telecomreview)).

A household survey reported in June 2025 records the urban and rural internet use gap, and no successor survey is held ([gap](2025-06-12 Rwanda hits 38% internet penetration, but cost still keeps millions offline)).

Cost is the constraint both sources name, and neither carries a tariff series against which affordability could be tracked.

summary: A [government network](2025-07-09-rdap-fast-track-2026-newtimes) carrying US$33.5m is named as a project subcomponent and has not moved in the base in twelve months.
developments:
It is named as a subcomponent of the acceleration project with a stated allocation and nothing else: no route, capacity, coverage or completion figure ([network](2025-07-09-rdap-fast-track-2026-newtimes)).

A named national system carrying that much money and generating no reporting for a year is the clearest instance in this unit of the reporting problem the acceleration project has generally.

summary: A [new subsea cable system](2026-07-09 Seacom plans 25,000km subsea cable from France to Singapore and South Africa) was announced in July 2026 with no timeline, and for a landlocked country the exposure is the terrestrial leg rather than the cable.
developments:
The system was announced in early July 2026 and no timeline was given ([cable](2026-07-09 Seacom plans 25,000km subsea cable from France to Singapore and South Africa)).

A landlocked country's exposure is backhaul, so this row moves only when the terrestrial leg is contracted. The cross-border terrestrial route recorded elsewhere in this report is the relevant instrument, and its live status rests on a vendor announcement.

summary: A [satellite reseller authorisation](2026-02-17-bsc-starlink-reseller-newtimes) was certified by the space agency in February 2026, on a partnership running since December 2025.
developments:
The reseller was certified in February 2026 and the partnership dates from December 2025; the held body is partial and flagged for verification ([authorisation](2026-02-17-bsc-starlink-reseller-newtimes)).

No subscriber count, tariff or coverage figure is published, so the authorisation records a licensing step rather than availability.

summary: A [national data centre](2026-03-19-water-policy-data-centres-newtimes) is named in the sector plan with no capacity, load or ownership figure published, and the country hosted no hyperscale facility as at March 2026.
developments:
The facility is named in the ministry's sector plan for 2024 to 2029 and no capacity, load or ownership figure is published anywhere the base holds ([centre](2026-03-19-water-policy-data-centres-newtimes), [plan](2025-01-01-minict-rwanda-ict-sector-strategic-plan-2024-2029)).

Data centre and cloud service directives issued in 2023 govern the national facility, and they are dated only by the sector plan because they carry no date of their own ([directives](2026-08-05-risa-data-center-and-cloud-services-directives)).

That is the whole of the domestic hosting record: one facility with no published capacity, governed by directives whose date has to be inferred.

summary: No [sovereign artificial-intelligence compute](2026-08-01-east-africa-ai-industry-hidden-dependency) is named — no national accelerator cluster and no sovereign cloud — and the only onshore compute the base can name is a foreign hybrid deployment.
developments:
No national accelerator cluster or sovereign artificial-intelligence cloud is named in anything held; the argument is a named analyst's, and its author sells sovereign infrastructure, which is stated here because it bears on the weight the claim can carry ([compute](2026-08-01-east-africa-ai-industry-hidden-dependency), [deployment](2026-04-17 Amazon Web Services launches Outposts in Rwanda. - Montjalinews)).

A second account reaches the same absence: no cluster, facility or hosted model is named, and what supports the finding is a dependency argument plus the absence of any contrary record ([dependency](2026-08-01-east-africa-ai-industry-hidden-dependency)).

African-founded cloud and artificial-intelligence infrastructure providers appear in a continental roundup rather than a market measure, with no capacity, customer count or domestic share stated ([providers](2026-08-26-four-african-cloud-startups-to-watch-2026)).

summary: No [data-centre water policy](2026-03-19-water-policy-data-centres-newtimes) is identified, and an analyst calls for early planning before capacity is built.
developments:
No instrument is identified and the call for early planning is an analyst's ([policy](2026-03-19-water-policy-data-centres-newtimes)).

It is the only country-specific energy source the base holds for this unit, which means the grid and water questions that the hosting ambition depends on are effectively unmeasured here.

summary: An [institute of computing](2026-08-03-rwanda-institute-of-computing-five-things) was approved by cabinet in July 2026 to open that September, with international university and vendor partnerships still to be established.
developments:
Cabinet approved it on 24 July 2026 for a September opening ([institute](2026-08-03-rwanda-institute-of-computing-five-things), [approval](2026-07-25-newtimes-rwanda-institute-of-computing)).

The partnerships that would supply its teaching are still to be established, and the coding academy becomes its sole feeder. A domestic training pipeline standing up at the same moment as the artificial-intelligence agency is the shape of this unit's answer to the compute and skills gap its own developers report.

progress: Mixed, an authority and an incident-response team in place while the skills appropriation executed at 11.5 per cent
summary: A [national cyber security authority](2026-06-30-rwa-2026-01-fp) is budgeted under the presidency for a third year, and the [standards and skills line](2026-06-30-rwa-2026-01-fq) executed at 11.5 per cent in 2024/25, the weakest of the country's digital programmes.
developments:
The authority is budgeted inside the presidency rather than a ministry, and its establishing law and enforcement powers are not held ([authority](2026-06-30-rwa-2026-01-fp), [cyberspace](2026-06-30-rwa-2026-01-fp)).

A national computer security incident response team published a profile in 2022 under the 2017 authority law; team membership is not public and no caseload or service-level figure is published ([team](2022-06-30-rw-csirt-rfc-2350-profile)).

The standards and skills appropriation executed at 11.5 per cent in 2024/25, the weakest execution among the country's digital programmes, and was appropriated again for 2026/27 ([skills](2026-06-30-rwa-2026-01-fq), [prior](2025-06-30-rwa-2025-01-fq)). A centre of excellence was inaugurated in October 2025 with no enrolment, throughput or funding figure published since ([centre](2025-10-03-cyber-security-centre-cyberhub-itweb)).

summary: A [national data-sharing platform](2025-09-27-data-sharing-platform-2026-newtimes) was phased for 2025 to 2026 with no go-live announced, and it is the interoperability gap the country's own analysts name most often.
developments:
The platform was phased for delivery across 2025 and 2026 and no go-live has been announced ([platform](2025-09-27-data-sharing-platform-2026-newtimes), [governance](2026-05-07 What will determine the success of Rwanda’s data governance push)).

The policy above it is approved and in implementation, and the architecture framework beside it is held as an excerpt. The missing piece is the one that would actually move data between systems, and it is the piece domestic commentary keeps returning to.

progress: Mixed, iris added to a three-modality biometric capture while the consent and access-log layer has no delivery evidence
summary: The [single digital identity](2026-06-09-accelerates-biometric-enrollment-biometricupdate) adds iris to face and ten fingerprints, and the [consent and access-log layer](2026-05-26-new-digital-id-you-control-everything-ktpress) has no stated go-live.
developments:
Nationwide registration launched in August 2025 and the capture now runs iris alongside face and ten fingerprints ([identity](2026-06-09-accelerates-biometric-enrollment-biometricupdate), [registration](2025-08-08 Rwanda National Identification Agency begins digital ID enrollment), [deadline](2026-03-26-govt-sets-2027-deadline-digital-id-newtimes)).

The consent and access-log layer is described as such with no go-live stated. It is the load-bearing safeguard in the design — the thing that would let a person see who has read their record — and it is the one component with no delivery evidence at all ([layer](2026-05-26-new-digital-id-you-control-everything-ktpress), [progress](2026-03-16 Digital IDs How registration is progressing so far)).

A system that adds a third biometric modality faster than it adds the log of who queries it has ordered its work in a particular way, and the statutory sunset of legacy documents falls before the safeguard is evidenced.

summary: [More than 8m people were registered](2026-08-17-newtimes-rwanda-digital-id-enrollment-8-million) by August 2026 against a June 2027 hard deadline, and registration and photographing are separate counts whose gap is unexplained.
developments:
More than 8m registrations were reported in August 2026, with biometric enrolment accelerating through the year ([enrolment](2026-08-17-newtimes-rwanda-digital-id-enrollment-8-million), [acceleration](2026-06-09-accelerates-biometric-enrollment-biometricupdate), [progress](2026-03-16 Digital IDs How registration is progressing so far)).

Registration and photographing are separate counts and the gap between them is not explained, which matters because the June 2027 deadline is statutory rather than administrative: on that date legacy documents cease to be valid whether or not the gap has closed.

The national identification appropriation outturned at 140.7 per cent of its allocation in 2024/25 and was appropriated again for 2026/27 ([appropriation](2026-06-30-rwa-2026-28-b9)); it is the digital line the fisc actually funds, against the flat data-protection line and the 11.5 per cent cyber-skills execution ([appropriation](2026-06-30-rwa-2026-28-b9), [prior](2025-06-30-rwa-2025-28-b9)).

summary: A [biometric SIM registration regulation](2024-08-09 Regulation Governing SIM Card Registration in Rwanda (RURA No.18-2024)) was issued in August 2024 and piloted the following month.
developments:
The regulation governs registration of subscriber cards and was piloted in September 2024 ([regulation](2024-08-09 Regulation Governing SIM Card Registration in Rwanda (RURA No.18-2024)), [pilot](2024-09-17 Rwanda conducts pilot to implement biometric SIM registration, verification)).

Nothing on file records completion, coverage or a link to the digital identity register, so whether the two biometric captures are one enrolment or two is not established here.

summary: All domestic interoperable retail payments [migrated to a national instant payment system](2026-07-14-migrates-retail-payments-ekash-itweb) by directive in July 2026, and the [interoperable transfer fee](2026-07-14-rwanda-bankers-association-ekash-interoperability) is a ceiling of RWF 20 rather than a flat charge.
developments:
Consumer launch was December 2025 and interoperability completed in July 2026, when a directive migrated all domestic interoperable retail payments onto the system ([migration](2026-07-14-migrates-retail-payments-ekash-itweb), [interoperability](2026-07-15-ekash-nationwide-interoperable-wearetech), [design](2025-03-10 Powering Rwanda's Payments Future How Mojaloop Enables RNDPS 2.0 and eKash)).

The fee is a maximum, not a flat charge, and it prices the interoperability layer only: the bankers' association's public notice puts it as a maximum with institutions free to offer lower or zero-fee options, applying to every transfer between banks and electronic money issuers ([fee](2026-07-14-rwanda-bankers-association-ekash-interoperability), [performance](2026-08-05-bnr-press-release-performance-of-ekash)).

The governing directive is not held: the central bank's document library was enumerated and carries neither it nor the public notice, and two sources give different issue dates for it, so its date is unestablished. What governs on-net tariffs is likewise unestablished ([scrutiny](2026-08-02-mtn-mobile-money-faces-scrutiny-over-fees-as-rwandas-digital-economy-expands), [launch](2026-07-27-rwanda-unifies-digital-payments-national-launch-ekash)).

progress: Mixed, active mobile money accounts and formal financial access both rising while the agent network lags and the second operator contracts
summary: [Active mobile money accounts](2026-06-29-rura-ict-sector-statistics-report-q1-2026) rose to the first quarter of 2026, while [accounts per agent](2026-06-29-rura-ict-sector-statistics-report-q1-2026) rose with the agent network lagging and the [second operator contracted](2026-07-31-ekash-airtel-money-struggles-rural-users).
developments:
The account series comes from the regulator's quarterly statistics, and the earlier figure is derived from the growth rate rather than printed ([accounts](2026-06-29-rura-ict-sector-statistics-report-q1-2026), [rural](2026-07-31-ekash-airtel-money-struggles-rural-users)).

Accounts per agent rose because the agent network grew more slowly than the account base, and the earlier figures there are implied from growth rates rather than separately held ([agents](2026-06-29-rura-ict-sector-statistics-report-q1-2026)).

The second operator contracted in the cash-in and cash-out layer, which is precisely the layer the new payment rail does not touch ([operator](2026-07-31-ekash-airtel-money-struggles-rural-users)). Formal financial access was reported at the payment system's national launch, and a second source puts inclusion higher on a different metric ([access](2026-07-27-rwanda-unifies-digital-payments-national-launch-ekash)).

summary: A bank and mobile operator launched a [joint digital loan and savings product](2026-08-02-bpr-bank-rwanda-and-mtn-momo-rwanda-launch-mofaya-digital-loan-and-savings-solution) in August 2026, and the mobile money platform [migrated to a cloud-native vendor platform](2026-08-21-tan-ericsson-mtn-momo-cloud-migration) across four markets.
developments:
The credit product launched on 2 August 2026, and the announcement names no regulator, consumer-protection arrangement or credit-data arrangement ([product](2026-08-02-bpr-bank-rwanda-and-mtn-momo-rwanda-launch-mofaya-digital-loan-and-savings-solution)).

The platform migration completed across four markets; the performance figures are the vendor's own and no downtime, cost or subscriber-impact figure is stated ([migration](2026-08-21-tan-ericsson-mtn-momo-cloud-migration)).

A credit product built on operator data and a platform moved onto a foreign vendor's cloud in the same month is the private half of the payments picture, and neither carries a regulatory statement.

summary: A [cross-border payment corridor pilot](2026-07-10 New Rwanda-Tanzania Payment Pilot could transform trade across East Africa) with a neighbour advanced a proof of concept at a technical meeting, with no launch date set.
developments:
The proof of concept was advanced at a technical meeting in July 2026 and no launch date is stated ([pilot](2026-07-10 New Rwanda-Tanzania Payment Pilot could transform trade across East Africa)).

It sits alongside two licence-passporting memoranda with other neighbours whose texts are unpublished. The country's cross-border payments record is three bilateral arrangements, none of them yet carrying a transaction the base can date.

summary: A [fully digital civil registration chain](2026-04-21-rwanda-counting-everything-nisr-ktpress) runs from hospitals to village administration, and the [system is documented as a foundation model](2026-08-13-birth-registration-emerges-as-foundation-for-digital-public-infrastructure) in published case studies.
developments:
Birth-registration completeness is reported in the 2025 vital statistics report, on a chain that runs digitally from hospitals through to village administration ([completeness](2026-04-21-rwanda-counting-everything-nisr-ktpress)).

The system is documented as a digital public infrastructure foundation model in published case studies; the account and its figures are those of the advocacy organisation that has worked on the system since 2016, and no government statement of the same figures is held ([case studies](2026-08-13-birth-registration-emerges-as-foundation-for-digital-public-infrastructure)).

That qualification matters at exactly the point the system is being held up as a model for others, and the immunisation registry recorded separately is integrated with it.

summary: [Business registration moved entirely online](2026-07-22-norebase-state-of-expansions-report) in January 2026, and the prior state is inferred from the source's own wording rather than stated.
developments:
Registration moved fully online in January 2026 on a market-expansion report's account ([platform](2026-07-22-norebase-state-of-expansions-report)).

No registration volume, processing time or fee is published, so what the move changed for a business is not measurable from what the base holds.

summary: A [district land correction exercise](2026-06-17-kayonza-land-correction-28000-titles-realrwanda) concluded in June 2026, with 222,423 boundary errors corrected across 825 villages nationally and the fee waived.
developments:
The district exercise concluded on 17 June 2026, part of a national correction in which 222,423 boundary errors were corrected across 825 villages with the fee waived ([exercise](2026-06-17-kayonza-land-correction-28000-titles-realrwanda), [disputes](2026-02-18-rwanda-land-disputes-ease-boundary-errors)).

The scale of the correction is the finding: a digitised cadastre that needed errors fixed at that volume was carrying them before the exercise, and nothing on file states how they arose.

The registry's capacity rests on a twinning arrangement with a foreign cadastral agency running 2022 to 2027, with nothing published on delivery ([twinning](2022-01-01-iati-se-0-se-6-15037-land-management-capacity-rwanda)).

summary: An [appeals process for the social registry](2026-08-03-rwanda-imibereho-social-registry-appeals) was reported on in August 2026, and the correction rate is the social affairs directorate's own figure.
developments:
The registry has an appeals process and the correction rate published for it comes from the directorate that runs the registry rather than from an independent review ([appeals](2026-08-03-rwanda-imibereho-social-registry-appeals)).

A social register with a working appeals route is more than most units in this frame can show. That the only measure of how well it works is the operator's own is the qualification.

summary: An [electronic immunisation registry](2026-07-30-implementation-strategies-to-promote-e-tracker-use-in-childhood-immunization-rwanda) replaced paper records across more than 500 facilities and integrates with civil registration, and a [national electronic medical record](2026-07-23-tbi-rwanda-health-data) has a blueprint but no rollout date.
developments:
A ministerial directive of October 2022 ended paper immunisation records, on a registry phased in from September 2019 to January 2020 across more than 500 facilities and integrated with civil registration and the identity agency in early 2022 ([registry](2026-07-30-implementation-strategies-to-promote-e-tracker-use-in-childhood-immunization-rwanda)).

The national electronic medical record is a blueprint drawn from one hospital build with no rollout date, and a 2025 analysis had described the system as already operating — the two accounts are not reconciled ([record](2026-07-23-tbi-rwanda-health-data)).

A national health intelligence centre launched in April 2025, and its latency and impact claims are partner-reported rather than independently verified ([centre](2026-07-23-tbi-rwanda-health-data), [funding](2026-07-21-rwanda-nhic-health-data-gates)).

summary: The [electronic billing machine has become an export](2026-07-30-rwanda-turns-digital-public-infrastructure-into-a-continental-growth-strategy), adopted by two neighbours with a third mid-adoption, and no revenue or licensing terms are disclosed.
developments:
Two neighbours have adopted the system and a third is mid-adoption, with no revenue, contract value or licensing terms disclosed for any adoption ([export](2026-07-30-rwanda-turns-digital-public-infrastructure-into-a-continental-growth-strategy), [transfer](2025-07-10-technology-transfer-rwanda-export-ktpress)).

A domestic revenue system exported to three states is the strongest evidence in this unit that the government-technology stack works, and the absence of any commercial terms is what stops it being evidence of a viable export business.

summary: The [government services platform](2026-07-30-rwanda-turns-digital-public-infrastructure-into-a-continental-growth-strategy) reported its scale at a national infrastructure day, against a hundred-plus services in 2021 as the only earlier figure held.
developments:
The scale figure comes from coverage of the national infrastructure day, and the only earlier held comparator is a hundred-plus services in 2021 ([platform](2026-07-30-rwanda-turns-digital-public-infrastructure-into-a-continental-growth-strategy)).

The electronic procurement platform is being adopted and co-developed by another state; a July meeting reports areas identified rather than agreements reached ([procurement](2026-07-30-rwanda-turns-digital-public-infrastructure-into-a-continental-growth-strategy), [meeting](2026-07-21-guinee-rwanda-explorent-nouveaux-projets-e-sante-ia)).

Both rows are the same shape: a working national system, reported through its export or its launch event rather than through a service, transaction or uptake series.

summary: A [local-government citizen platform](2025-10-15-mbaza-local-gov-platform-newtimes) opened a capital-city trial in January 2026, and the source is a partial body.
developments:
The trial opened on 27 January 2026, with trial detail coming from syndicated coverage of the same session rather than from a separate account ([platform](2025-10-15-mbaza-local-gov-platform-newtimes)).

No district count, service list or usage figure is published, so the platform is recorded here as a trial and nothing more.

progress: Mixed, school connectivity advancing while one of the two education-technology appropriations fell
summary: [School internet connectivity](2026-03-31-connecting-812-schools-edtech-ktpress) advanced at a March 2026 dialogue against a government target of 80 per cent, and nothing has been published since.
developments:
Connectivity was reported at an education-technology dialogue in March 2026 against a government target of 80 per cent, and nothing has been published on it in the five months since ([connectivity](2026-03-31-connecting-812-schools-edtech-ktpress)).

The education-technology integration appropriation grows in the 2026/27 finance law and is the one education-technology line that does ([integration](2026-06-30-rwa-2026-14-70), [prior](2025-06-30-rwa-2025-14-70)).

The second education-technology line fell; its 2024/25 year had spent 252.4 per cent of a revised allocation, so the fall is against a base that was itself heavily overspent ([second line](2026-06-30-rwa-2026-14-es), [baseline](2024-06-26-rwa-2024-14-es)).

summary: A [primary-care artificial-intelligence health pilot](2026-01-22 Gates Foundation and OpenAI Commit $50m to AI-Powered Health Systems in Africa) was announced in January 2026 with this country first, on the announcing parties' own figure.
developments:
The pilot was announced on 22 January 2026 under a US$50m commitment across African health systems, with this country the first ([pilot](2026-01-22 Gates Foundation and OpenAI Commit $50m to AI-Powered Health Systems in Africa), [horizon](2026-01-01-gates-foundation-rwa-2026-horizon1000-ai-health-bw08)).

The figure is the announcing parties' own. No deployment site, patient count, evaluation design or clinical-governance arrangement is published, and it lands in a health system whose national medical record is still a blueprint.

summary: A [code-switching African voice model](2026-08-26-intron-sahara-v2-5-code-switching-voice-model) covers the country's languages but was built elsewhere, and an [artificial-intelligence scaling hub](2026-06-10 Rwanda Launches Dedicated AI Agency to Drive Investment and Innovation) has a funding total and no dated commitment.
developments:
The voice model was built outside the country and is named here for the languages it covers; no local deployment, accuracy benchmark or user figure is published ([model](2026-08-26-intron-sahara-v2-5-code-switching-voice-model)).

The scaling hub reaches the base as a single secondary mention carrying a funding total with no dated commitment behind it ([hub](2026-06-10 Rwanda Launches Dedicated AI Agency to Drive Investment and Innovation)).

A continental artificial-intelligence fund was announced at the capital's summit in April 2025 and nothing has moved on it since ([fund](2025-05-13 Optimism but uncertainty over Africa's AI Declaration)). Against a country that convenes the continent's artificial-intelligence diplomacy, the base holds no model, cluster or dataset built here.

summary: No [national artificial-intelligence risk-assessment and harms-monitoring body](2026-07-06-undp-small-states-big-signals-ai-trust-safety) is held, on engagements run from November 2025 to March 2026.
developments:
The finding rests on qualitative workshops rather than a survey, and the report claims no representativeness for them ([engagements](2026-07-06-undp-small-states-big-signals-ai-trust-safety), [landscape](2026-01-01-world-bank-radu-global-landscape-national-ai-strategies)).

The country holds an artificial-intelligence policy, is standing up an agency and co-chairs a global commission, and the function that would identify and monitor harms domestically is the one with no body attached.

summary: The [dominant operator returned to profit](2026-05-11-mtn-rwanda-return-to-profit-techcabal) in the quarter to March 2026, and [information and communication employment](2026-07-20-rwanda-tech-jobs-lfs) is the fastest-growing sector in the labour force survey off a very small base.
developments:
The results are the operator's own reported figures and the held body is a partial capture ([results](2026-05-11-mtn-rwanda-return-to-profit-techcabal)).

Employment in the sector grew fastest of any in the second-quarter labour force survey, off a very small base — which is the qualification that decides how much the growth rate means ([employment](2026-07-20-rwanda-tech-jobs-lfs)).

There is no domestic manufacture, assembly or hardware production of any kind in the base for this unit.

summary: A [financial technology centre](2026-03-13-fintech-centre-sets-stage-itweb) was inaugurated in March 2026, and an [innovation city](2022-01-01-africa50-rwa-kigali-innovation-city-2022-kigali-innovation-city-kic-technopark-ppp) broke ground in September 2024 on an equity ticket never publicly disclosed.
developments:
The centre was inaugurated on 12 March 2026, and the sector count and inclusion figure attached to it are the minister's ([centre](2026-03-13-fintech-centre-sets-stage-itweb), [hub role](2026-05-14-strengthens-fintech-hub-role-itweb)).

The innovation city broke ground in September 2024 under a public-private partnership; the equity ticket is imputed and was never publicly disclosed ([city](2022-01-01-africa50-rwa-kigali-innovation-city-2022-kigali-innovation-city-kic-technopark-ppp)).

Neither carries an occupancy, tenant or output figure, so both are recorded as built rather than as working.

summary: An [innovation fund](2026-07-20-rwanda-tech-jobs-lfs) had backed twelve companies by 2024, reported second-hand with no fund document held.
developments:
Twelve companies had been backed by 2024, on a second-hand report ([fund](2026-07-20-rwanda-tech-jobs-lfs)).

No fund document, size, mandate or portfolio is held. Against a national ambition that runs to an innovation city, a financial technology centre and an artificial-intelligence agency, twelve companies is the only portfolio figure the base can state.

summary: The [digital ambassador programme](2022-01-01-koica-rwa-digital-ambassador-2022-project-for-enhancing-digital-literacy-through) concluded its financing phase in May 2026 with no successor financing held.
developments:
The programme was to be expanded to all 2,148 cells under the acceleration project, and its financing phase concluded in May 2026 ([programme](2022-01-01-koica-rwa-digital-ambassador-2022-project-for-enhancing-digital-literacy-through), [expansion](2025-07-09-rdap-fast-track-2026-newtimes)).

No successor financing is held. A national digital-literacy programme reaching every cell is the kind of instrument a statutory identity deadline depends on, and it lost its funding a year before that deadline falls.

summary: [Artificial-intelligence trust and safety training for officials](2026-08-01-undp-rwanda-q2-ai-trust-safety-canada-support) was delivered in the quarter reported August 2026, on the funder's own quarterly newsletter.
developments:
The training was delivered with donor support and reported in the funder's own quarterly newsletter, which is the only account held ([training](2026-08-01-undp-rwanda-q2-ai-trust-safety-canada-support)).

No participant count, curriculum or department is named. It is the only civil-service digital training in the base for this unit.

summary: A [national artificial-intelligence literacy programme for teachers](2026-08-03-muhizi-njila-africa-ai-risk-misread-rwanda-execution-stack) completed a first phase at the end of 2025, asserted in a diplomat-authored opinion piece.
developments:
The first phase is reported complete at end-2025, and the assertion sits in an opinion piece written by a diplomat with no ministry primary held behind it ([programme](2026-08-03-muhizi-njila-africa-ai-risk-misread-rwanda-execution-stack)).

No teacher count, curriculum, school coverage or evaluation is published. On the evidence held this is a claim about a programme rather than a record of one.

summary: A [coding academy](2021-09-02-minecofin-rwanda-coding-academy-koica-frw-71-billion) becomes the sole feeder to the new institute of computing, and an [inclusive digital transformation centre](2022-01-01-mcf-rwa-cmu-digital-2022-cmu-africa-center-for-inclusive-digital-transformation) is the largest single training commitment the base holds.
developments:
The academy runs under a record of discussion signed in September 2021 and no enrolment figure is held after that date; it becomes the sole feeder to the institute of computing ([academy](2021-09-02-minecofin-rwanda-coding-academy-koica-frw-71-billion), [institute](2026-08-03-rwanda-institute-of-computing-five-things)).

The inclusive digital transformation centre runs under a foundation partnership signed in 2022 and is the largest single training commitment the base holds for this country ([centre](2022-01-01-mcf-rwa-cmu-digital-2022-cmu-africa-center-for-inclusive-digital-transformation)).

Neither carries a graduate, placement or completion figure at any date, so the pipeline into the new institute cannot be sized.

summary: An [African academic security operation centre](2026-08-24-cmu-africa-academic-security-operation-center) operates through a university network based here, with no monitored-estate, incident or staffing figure published.
developments:
The centre runs through a university network based in the country ([centre](2026-08-24-cmu-africa-academic-security-operation-center)), and a continental research and education partnership carries a grant of about US$9m from 2022 to 2027 with no progress or outturn report held at any date ([partnership](2022-01-01-koica-rwa-digital-ambassador-2022-project-for-enhancing-digital-literacy-through)).

An academic security operation centre is an unusual asset for a country of this size, and the absence of any operational figure means it cannot be counted as national cyber capacity in the readiness assessment recorded elsewhere.

summary: A [universal access fund](2023-05-12-rwanda-presidential-order-025-01-2023-universal-access-fund) was re-established by presidential order in 2023 with no separate legal personality, and its owed annual activity report is not held for any year.
developments:
The order was gazetted on 15 May 2023, repealing the 2004 order. The fund has no separate legal personality and its staff sit inside the regulator, and the annual activity report owed to the regulatory board by 30 September is not held for any year ([order](2023-05-12-rwanda-presidential-order-025-01-2023-universal-access-fund), [regulator](2021-01-01-rura-annual-report-2020-2021), [project](2025-07-09-rdap-fast-track-2026-newtimes)).

A smart-device affordability fund is at design stage with a market assessment pending ([devices](2025-07-09-rdap-fast-track-2026-newtimes)), and the acceleration project's inclusion components — the device fund, the ambassador expansion, and school and clinic connectivity — sit under a briefing to parliament in July 2025 ([components](2025-07-09-rdap-fast-track-2026-newtimes), [appraisal](2021-11-30-wb-rwa-001-digital-acceleration-project)).

Every instrument aimed at the divide is either unreported, at design stage, or inside a project that last reported in 2025.

summary: The [statistics programme appropriation](2026-06-30-rwa-2026-10-52) fell as the programme moved between ministries, and the national statistics function is 87 per cent externally financed.
developments:
The appropriation fell in the 2026/27 finance law and the programme moved between ministries in the same period ([appropriation](2026-06-30-rwa-2026-10-52), [prior](2025-06-30-rwa-2025-12-52)).

The function is 87 per cent externally financed ([financing](2026-06-30-rwa-2026-10-52)). The statistics office also holds governance of the national data-sharing policy, so the body that owns the country's data governance is the one whose own funding is almost entirely donor-carried.

summary: No [national open-data portal, catalogue or policy](2026-05-07 What will determine the success of Rwanda’s data governance push) is on file, against a data-sharing policy that runs open by default.
developments:
Nothing is held: no portal, no catalogue, no policy ([absence](2026-05-07 What will determine the success of Rwanda’s data governance push)).

The data-sharing policy is open by default with a safe-access framework, so the country has adopted the principle for government-to-government sharing and has published nothing that opens data to anyone outside government ([policy](2025-10-27 Introduction to the Rwanda National Data Sharing Policy)).

summary: A [national satellite data programme](2026-08-10-itweb-planet-rwanda-national-satellite-data-program) was announced with a commercial imagery provider in August 2026, and no contract or appropriation is held.
developments:
The programme was announced jointly by the vendor and government on 10 August 2026, and no contract or appropriation is held ([programme](2026-08-10-itweb-planet-rwanda-national-satellite-data-program)).

The space programme appropriation's last held record is the 2024/25 finance law and it is the only satellite-data source the base holds beyond the announcement ([appropriation](2024-06-26-rwa-2024-01-f5)).

So a national imagery capability is being stood up on a commercial arrangement nobody outside the parties has seen, against a budget line the base cannot follow past 2024/25.

summary: A [three-year memorandum with a frontier artificial-intelligence firm](2026-02-17-anthropic-rwanda-mou-ai-health-education) covers health and education, a [hyperscaler partnership](2026-08-13-rwanda-google-ai-partnership-digital-transformation) is at scoping, and a [hybrid cloud deployment](2026-04-17 Amazon Web Services launches Outposts in Rwanda. - Montjalinews) is the only onshore compute the base can name.
developments:
The vendor memorandum was signed on 17 February 2026, non-binding, the first multi-sector government agreement of its kind in Africa; the vendor's own announcement is the only primary held ([memorandum](2026-02-17-anthropic-rwanda-mou-ai-health-education), [deal](2026-03-04 U.S.-based AI firm Anthropic bags first multi-sector government deal in Africa despite policy pressures at home)).

A two-day working session with a hyperscaler is the whole of the second record: the terms on which national data would sit with a foreign provider are not addressed in it ([scoping](2026-08-13-rwanda-google-ai-partnership-digital-transformation)).

The hybrid cloud deployment launched in April 2026 with deployment count and host facilities undisclosed, and it is the only onshore compute the base can name for this country ([deployment](2026-04-17 Amazon Web Services launches Outposts in Rwanda. - Montjalinews), [first](2026-04-01 Rwanda hosts first AWS Outposts)). Three American arrangements carry the compute, the frontier model and the scoping, and no review framework governs any of them.

summary: No [bilateral technology instrument with China](2026-01-19 Rwanda, China forge technology alliance) is held, and the record is an exploratory ambassadorial meeting in January 2026.
developments:
The meeting was exploratory and no instrument came out of it that the base holds ([meeting](2026-01-19 Rwanda, China forge technology alliance)).

Surveillance supply is asserted only at continent level with no national contract named, which is worth stating plainly: the base has no evidence of Chinese technology procurement by this government at any date.

summary: No [European adequacy decision](2026-05-15 Africa–Europe Cooperation on AI Governance Report) has been sought or granted, on a desk review whose counts are round estimates single-sourced to a secondary tracker.
developments:
None has been sought or granted ([adequacy](2026-05-15 Africa–Europe Cooperation on AI Governance Report)).

The country holds a data protection law fully in force since 2023 and a named supervisory authority, so the absence is not for want of a regime. Nothing on file records an application, an assessment or a stated intention to seek one.
